newsitem.title: FRANCE: Euro-MPs approve new ship safety rules.
newsitem.headline: Euro-MPs approve new ship safety rules.

text.p: Accidents at sea caused by sub-standard navigational or safety equipment should become rarer in European Union waters after the European Parliament approved new marine safety rules on Thursday.

The parliament approved a draft directive which requires all vessels entering EU ports to respect the same high safety standards for radiocommunications equipment, lifeboats and life jackets, fire extinguishers and other pieces of equipment - COM(95)269.
EU transport ministers provisionally cleared this first piece of EU law on the safety and efficacity of marine equipment on July 17. It needed parliament's approval to become law.
The new rules oblige member states to check that all vessels entering their ports carry certificates which guarantee that their equipment meets minimum standards.
There may be further checks if the authorities doubt the vessel's condition.
The directive on equipment safety leaves it to member states to decide how often they should carry out checks.
While generally very satisfied with the text approved by ministers, Euro-MPs called for three amendments.
Parliament said the directive should insist that all vessel safety inspectors be entirely independent of the equipment manufacturers and suppliers.
Euro-MPs also said the text should be reworded to make explicitly clear that its provisions cover radiocommunications equipment, which is also the subject of a separate EU directive.
Finally, they recommended giving the European Commission the power to administer the directive, helped by member state representatives playing a purely advisory role.
